answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor 1 (AGENTS.md:2418 and roleKeepDrainRetryCap's doc): both still stated the rule 628cb287 deleted - a failed read waited out 'while the holder is live' - where the code now retries on any pass, the first included, while the role's cached claim names a session, live or lapsed, and ends at Debug otherwise. A reader who trusts 'live' misses the lapsed-claim case.
answersReviewFindings.fix: Both now state the rule as handOverKeptRole's own doc states it, naming the cached claim and 'live or lapsed' and dropping 'while the holder is live'.
answersReviewFindings.test: No test; prose. bun scripts/semantic-line-breaks.ts packages/envoy/AGENTS.md is silent and check-private-names.sh is clean.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor 2 (role_keep_handover_test.go:659): a report-and-count that checks nothing, since the line above has already failed the test unless err == nil and reportKeptRoleDrain(cfg, role, nil) returns at once; and the rest of the test repeats TestAHandoverRetriesALaneHeadReadThatFailedOnItsFirstPass step for step.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The two are one table test, TestAHandoverRetriesALaneHeadReadThatFailedOnlyForAClaimedRole, over claimed, wantErr, wantRetried and wantErrorLines, with the dead check gone. The claimed row still proves the retry, its elapsed time and the Error line; the unclaimed row still proves the single read, the quick end and the silence, and that silence is now counted over every errorLine in the listener log rather than over what reportKeptRoleDrain(nil) would have written, so it asserts the handover's whole quiet rather than a tautology.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor 3 (role_keep_handover_test.go:694): the reflect/unsafe swap of the session registry's private watcher field written three times, here, at :473-476 and in api_test.go:1009-1012.
answersReviewFindings.fix: One swapSessionBucket(t, sessions, wrap) in api_test.go, called by stallSessionReads, countSessionBucketReads and failTheNextSessionRead; the reflect, unsafe and kvwatch imports are gone from role_keep_handover_test.go, so a rename of that field breaks one place.
answersReviewFindings.test: No new test: the three callers are themselves the proof, and all of them run in the suite.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor 4 (role_keep_handover_test.go:700): failed.Load() proves some read of the session bucket failed, not that the handover's own holder resolution took the failure and was retried; another reader could spend it and the test would pass having exercised nothing.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The test pins the pause instead: only the handover's own failed read earns roleKeepDrainRetryPause, so asserting elapsed >= roleKeepDrainRetryPause says the handover's resolution took the failure. The reviewer's first remedy, asserting the retry's Debug line, is not available here: the harness logger is logging.NewWithWriter, fixed at slog.LevelInfo, so no Debug line reaches harness.logs, and internal/logging is outside this change.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestAHandoverOfAClaimedRoleRetriesAHolderResolutionThatFailed, tightened. At a4b9ededf432 it fails with 'the handover of role kept-holder-read-failed ended 2.38908ms in, inside the first pause of 1s a failed read earns: the read that failed was another reader's, not its own resolution of the holder'; that revision cannot compile this branch's test file, so the run used a standalone file with the assertions copied verbatim.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor 5 (role_keep.go:533): retry() carried a read error out of any claimed role's handover, the error of a context that ended included, so a listener shutdown cancelling a sweep's handover mid-resolution logged 'listener kept role drain failed' at Error, where before 628cb287 it ended at Debug. An alert on that line would fire on every deploy.
answersReviewFindings.fix: retry() returns false when ctx.Err() != nil, after its Debug line and before the claim read, so a read whose only failure is the handover's own context ending carries nothing out and the handover ends as the loop's own ctx.Err() exits do. A read that genuinely failed still sets readErr and is still reported at Error.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestAHandoverReportsAHolderReadThatFailedAndNotOneItsShutdownCancelled, both halves: /failed, a session-bucket read that never answers on a claimed role, still ends with an error and one Error line; /cancelled, where the bucket read ends the handover's own context from inside the read, reports nothing with zero Error lines. At the committed code the /cancelled half fails with 'the handover of role kept-shutdown-cancelled reported read role holder session: ... context canceled, want an error reported: false'.
